newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to increase aid to shipbuilding sector.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to increase aid to shipbuilding sector.

text.p: Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers intends to raise government support to the Dutch shipbuilding sector by 10 million guilders, his ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
"This will take the amount available in 1996 to support Dutch shipbuilders to a total of 40 million guilders," it added.
The maximum subsidy percentages of 4.5 percent for small seagoing vessels and nine percent for large ships will remain unchanged.
The ministry said the amount will be raised as a European Union (EU) guideline on this subject was extended until the end of 1997.
This guideline was prolonged as the OECD shipbuilding agreement, which was aimed at cutting subsidies to this sector, could not be implemented because it was not ratified by the U.S.

The EU guideline enabled member states to coninue supporting their shipbuilders but this was expected to end by October. Given the extension, the Dutch subsidy will be increased to cover the last three months of the year, the ministry said.
"It is expected that in November -- after the U.S. (presidential) elections -- there will be more clarity on the U.S. position," the ministry said.
After that a decision will be taken on the Dutch state aid to the shipbuilding sector in 1997, it added.
